pr.title: GVN: Use a VnIndex in Address projection.
pr.description:
The current implementation of address projections is inconsistent. Indexing semantically relies on the index' value, but the implementation uses the index' place. This PR fixes that by using `ProjectionElem<VnIndex, Ty<'tcx>>` instead of the raw `PlaceElem<'tcx>`.

This is a more principled fix than the workaround in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/145030.

pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.summary: GVN must represent indexed address projections by the index's VnIndex value, not by the raw Place/local, so later overwrites of the index local cannot change which element an address denotes.
analysis.originalLogic: GVN represented a reference/raw-pointer value as `Value::Address { place: Place<'tcx>, kind, provenance }`, after `simplify_place_projection`. Later dereference/projection of that address reused/simplified the stored `Place`. For `ProjectionElem::Index(local)`, the `Place` identifies a local, not the index value at the time the address was created. The old code also had a `from_non_ssa_index` bailout, but the address still carried a raw `Place`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Treating an address's `Index(local)` projection as stable and later projecting/reusing it as if it still denoted the same index value. If `local` is overwritten between address creation and dereference, the stored `Place`'s `Index` can denote a different element than the one indexed when the address was formed. The fix captures the index as `ProjectionElem<VnIndex, Ty<'tcx>>` instead of a raw `PlaceElem<'tcx>`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR containing references or raw pointers to dynamically indexed arrays/slices (`&a[i]`, `&raw a[i]`), especially where the index local is mutable/non-SSA or is overwritten between borrow creation and a later dereference/projection. Repeated or equal-valued arrays can mask wrong index selection.
analysis.trigger: `Rvalue::Ref` or `Rvalue::RawPtr` creates `Value::Address` from a place whose projection contains `ProjectionElem::Index(local)`, and GVN later simplifies a dereference/projection of that address after `local` has been assigned a new value.
preconditions: GVN constructs a Value::Address from a borrow or raw-pointer place containing a dynamic Index projection.
The Index projection refers to a local, and that local's value is later changed or is otherwise not stable at the later use point.
GVN later simplifies a dereference or projection of that address.
For an observable test, the array/slice elements at the old and new index differ.
pitfalls: Do not equate an Index projection's local-place identity with the index value; the local may be overwritten after the borrow was formed.
Do not conflate this with borrow restrictions or shared-borrow freeze reasoning; the index is evaluated when the address is created, and the separate hazard is a later overwrite of the index local.
An SSA/non-SSA guard by itself is insufficient if the address still stores a raw Place rather than the index's VnIndex.
Address projections must not contain Deref; the fix separates the base (`AddressBase::Local` or `AddressBase::Deref`) from the remaining projection.

A missing optimization is not necessarily a bug: the new `index_place` test expects the dereference to remain unchanged when the captured index value cannot safely be expressed using the current index local.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused `tests/mir-opt` custom-MIR tests using `#[custom_mir(dialect = \"runtime\")]` and `EMIT_MIR`. Construct two functions differing only in whether the index local is overwritten: in both, take `elem = &array[idx1]`; in the hazard case execute `idx1 = idx2` before `RET = *elem`. The overwritten case must preserve `*elem` (as in the added `gvn_repeat.index_place` diff) or otherwise use the old index value, never the new local value. Use distinct array elements and a runtime assertion so a wrong-index rewrite is observable; the patch's `[0; 5]` assertion does not distinguish indices. Also check the optimized MIR directly with `CHECK`/`CHECK-NOT`, as in `dereference_indexing` where the expectation moved from `_9 = copy (*_3);` to `_9 = copy _1[_4];`.
